Opera today launched two new features for its desktop browser: optional vertical tabs, and expanded Google Lens integration. Details below.

Opera One gets two updates

In a blog post published today, Opera announced two updates for its Opera One browser.

The first is an increasingly common browser interface option: vertical tabs. It moves the traditional horizontal top tab bar to a stacked display on the side, with adjustable width for the tab column.

Opera said: "With vertical tabs, you can see the site favicons for your tabs, and most importantly, you can see the full tab titles, making it easy to identify each tab." In fact, users can choose to display full tab names, or switch to a mode showing only favicons, thereby freeing up more space for webpage content.

Vertical tabs can be enabled in Settings, under "Browser > Tabs".

In addition, Opera One has further expanded its previous integration with Google Lens. Opera stated:

"Google Lens has been present in Opera One for some time, but we have made it easier to use and expanded its capabilities. You can now perform image searches directly in the search bar on Opera's start page, as Google Lens is already integrated into the search bar. In addition, you can conduct image searches using local files or by pasting images from the clipboard. Simply click the Google Lens icon in the search bar, and a dialog will pop up where you can provide images by uploading a file, drag and drop, pasting from the clipboard, or entering an image URL. Search results will be displayed in your current tab."
